title: Resolving the fragmentation of high line-mass filaments with ALMA: the integral shaped filament in Orion A
question: What are the fragmentation length scales of the Orion A integral shaped filament, is there a preferred fragmentation scale or grouping of cores, and how do these relate to the young stellar population?

data.bands: 3 mm continuum (plus C18O line, not used)

what.value: Herschel column density map of Orion A

evidence.quote: We refer to (cite: stu15) for the details of the map.
(cite: meg12) for the disks and (cite: fur16) for the protostars

what.value: ISF density profile and line-mass used in model comparison

evidence.quote: (cite: stu15prep) have evaluated the (cylindric) density profile of the ISF to be 17 M$_\odot$ pc$^{-3} (r / \mathrm{pc})^{-13/8}$

recipe.method: Joint 7-m+12-m mosaic cleaning with natural weighting and box masks
2D Gaussian fitting with gaussclumps after median-filter background subtraction
key_parameters: Threshold 3 x rms = 0.23 mJy/beam rms; filter width 10''

recipe.goal: Classify cores as protostellar or starless
recipe.method: Cross-match core centroids with HOPS protostars and disks within 2''; reclassify four disk matches as protostars based on chance-alignment probability
Optically thin dust emission M = F d^2 / (B(T) kappa)
key_parameters: T = 20 K; d = 420 pc; kappa = 0.1 (nu/1000 GHz)^1.5 cm2/g

recipe.method: Mean, median and CDFs of projected nearest neighbour separations for cores, protostars and disks
Landy-Szalay estimator with Monte Carlo random samples and Gaussian density estimator
key_parameters: 10 000 random realisations with N=43 points; smoothing FWHM 5'' (20'' for large scales)

recipe.method: Core surface density map smoothed with 40'' Gaussian kernel; compared with Herschel peaks; Jeans and cylindrical fragmentation scales computed
assumptions: Inclination angle of zero; spherical structures for density

evidence.quote: Running gaussclumps resulted in detection of 43 compact objects from the ALMA map.
our dense core catalog consists of 26 protostellar cores and 17 starless cores.
The masses of the cores span 0.2-2.6 M$_\odot$

answer_key.quantity: Mean nearest neighbour separation, all cores

evidence.quote: it shows significant grouping below 17 000 AU and strong grouping below $\sim$6 000 AU.
62 000 $\pm$ 19 000 AU when considering the six largest groups

answer_key.quantity: Herschel column density peak mean separation

evidence.quote: the density of $\sim10^5$ cm$^{-3}$ and the fragmentation scale of $\sim$10 000 AU follows.
the $FWHM$$\approx$0.06 pc follows, yielding the fragmentation scale of $\sim$40 000 AU.

not_stated_but_needed: Clean threshold, niter, cell size, image size and mosaic gridding
Exact gaussclumps parameter file beyond Thresh and filter width (e.g. other FWHMBeam, Rms, fit-failure settings)
Exact HOPS catalog versions (Furlan 2016 was submitted)
Area used for random placement and boundary treatment in the Monte Carlo
missing_for_reproduction: Core catalog is in the paper table, so downstream stats can be redone
score_reason: Public ALMA data and fully listed core catalog, with main gaussclumps settings given, but imaging parameters and the protostar catalog details are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, a core catalog table and stated gaussclumps settings, and numeric results (43 cores, 2-pt scales) that can be redone.
